caption:
A false positive is not a shrug. It is a cost.

Every time a flagged change turns out to be nothing — a parked vehicle, a shift in vegetation, a shadow the algorithm misread — someone spent fuel, time, and attention chasing it. Do that enough times and the next real alert gets a slower response, because the desk has learned to discount the system.

That is why a tasking and alert pipeline is judged on precision, not just sensitivity. A system that flags everything catches everything and is trusted by no one. The discipline is knowing what confidence level a flag deserves before it reaches a commander's desk — and saying so.

Ground truth is what closes the loop. Until someone confirms what the imagery showed, every flag is a lead, not a fact.
